title: Why an Airport Sandwich Costs $18 (You're a Captive Customer)
alts: Why Airport Food Is So Expensive (It's Not Just Greed)
Dave Paid $25 for a Sandwich and Water. Here's Why.
line1: Why does a sandwich cost $18 at the airport? Dave paid $25 for lunch at the gate, and we found out exactly where that money goes.
summary: Dave buys one sandwich and a bottle of water at the gate and the bill hits $25. We break down why: you're a legal 'captive customer' the moment you clear security, a setup that only really started after 9/11 changed who can walk to the gate. The airport takes a real cut of every sale (a median 12.8% of food & beverage revenue, more for gift shops), on top of genuinely higher costs like TSA badging and screened deliveries, plus a monthly minimum guarantee written into most concession contracts. A 'street pricing' rule is supposed to cap markups near the outside price, but enforcement is spotty. We also explain why your water bottle gets confiscated at security, only for a new one to be sold to you a few feet later, and show simple ways to spend near $0 at the gate next time.
